description: We are a team of video game designers.
summary:
Our project is a video game about sustaining life on Mars. The game aims to give a simplified demonstration of the challenges that astronauts face to sustain life in mars to young audiences.
The video game requires the player to maintain food supply and power supply in mars by harvesting crops, and fixing solar panels that degrade over time.
The demo puts the player under the pressure of trying to keep food and power supplies in check over a small amount of time to give them an idea of how challenging it is to sustain life on mars.
details:
Our project, Redmission, aims to simplify complex challenges that astronauts will face when trying to sustain life on mars, especially the mental pressure that they go through during their missions.

Though our project is just a prototype/demo that can be added on, it still uses a collection of systems that work together to try and achieve the intended goal of the project, such as the farming/planting system that grows plants on a grid over time, which if left unchecked got rot. Similarly, solar panels are also arranged in a grid, but the degrade over time, therefore, their efficiency decreases over time and so does the power output. Therefore, the player must be quick in deciding which action they should take next: Should they go fix the solar panels to maintain a consistent power supply or should they harvest the crops before they rot?

To produce the solution/project we used 3 main tools: Unity 6 game engine, Visual Studio 2022 (Community edition), and Blender. We used the Unity editor to create the game whereas the Visual Studio IDE was used in scripting/programming/implementing the algorithms, systems, and controllers using the C# programming language to write those scripts. In the other hand we used Blender to create the 3D models and visuals used in the project in addition to some assets from the Unity asset store to design the 3D visuals of our game.

Finally, we had to consider the details of how we are going to implement the algorithms that are supposed to make the game work, and how we are going to use the resources given to us by NASA to achieve our intended goal. Additionally, time played a crucial role in limiting our scope, so we had to discard some ideas that we wanted to be in our game.
